ledger.sentence: An echocardiogram is a scan that uses ultrasound, high-frequency sound waves, to produce moving pictures of the heart.
ledger.note: NHS/MedlinePlus: ultrasound used to create pictures of the heart.

ledger.sentence: An ultrasound probe covered in gel is placed on the chest in the standard test.
ledger.note: Gel and transducer on chest supported; "water-based" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: The most common type is the transthoracic echocardiogram, in which the probe is placed over the chest.
ledger.note: NHS: most common type is transthoracic, transducer placed on chest.

ledger.sentence: A transoesophageal echocardiogram uses a probe that passes down the throat and gives more detailed pictures of the heart than the standard test.
ledger.note: NHS: probe passed down the throat, more detailed view of the heart.

ledger.sentence: Doctors may use it when the standard test has not shown enough detail.
ledger.note: RBHT (NHS trust): generally used when a chest echo cannot give enough information.

ledger.sentence: A stress echocardiogram is a transthoracic scan done during exercise on a treadmill or exercise bike, or after a medicine that has a similar effect on the heart.
ledger.note: NHS: treadmill or exercise bike, or medicine with similar effect.

ledger.sentence: For some echocardiograms, saline or a special dye is injected into a vein to help show the heart more clearly.
ledger.note: Retrieved (likely NHLBI/MedlinePlus, US): saline or special dye injected into a vein for some echoes. "Harmless" and "clearer image" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: A stress echocardiogram may be recommended if a heart problem is triggered by physical activity.
ledger.note: NHS: stress echo may be recommended when a heart problem is triggered by physical activity.

ledger.sentence: For the transoesophageal test, the back of the throat is numbed with an anaesthetic spray.
ledger.note: NHS: throat numbed with spray for TOE.

ledger.sentence: A sedative may be given to help the person relax.
ledger.note: NHS: a sedative given to help you relax; "very drowsy but not asleep" and "people can ask" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Avoiding food for several hours beforehand may be needed for this version.
ledger.note: NHS: may need to avoid eating for several hours before TOE.

ledger.sentence: Afterwards the throat may be sore, and this should pass within one or two days.
ledger.note: NHS: throat may be sore afterwards, passing within 1 to 2 days.

ledger.sentence: An NHS trust says a transoesophageal echocardiogram can look at the heart valves and heart muscle, and check for blood clots and tears in the aorta.
ledger.note: RBHT: can look at valves and heart muscle, clots, aortic tears. Heart muscle after a heart attack not retrieved; source is an NHS trust not nhs.uk page.

ledger.sentence: An NHS trust says it can help guide surgeons during some heart procedures.
ledger.note: RBHT: can guide surgeons during procedures such as mitral valve surgery; "plan surgery" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: The British Heart Foundation says an echocardiogram uses sound waves to build up a picture of the heart and its structures, such as the valves.
ledger.note: BHF: sound waves build a picture of the heart and its structures such as valves. Size and pumping not on BHF page in retrieved text (patent only).

ledger.sentence: It describes the test as an important investigation for anyone with suspected heart failure, heart valve problems or cardiomyopathy, a disease of the heart muscle.
ledger.note: BHF: important investigation for anyone with suspected heart failure, heart valve problems or cardiomyopathy.

ledger.sentence: Like other ultrasound scans, which the NHS says do not use radiation, an echocardiogram uses sound waves.
ledger.note: BHF: bubble echo quick and painless. No-radiation wording for echo not retrieved; NHS says ultrasound scans do not use radiation.

ledger.sentence: The NHS says some people may be able to talk to a doctor about the result on the day, but most people wait a few weeks.
ledger.note: NHS: may be able to talk to a doctor on the day, but most people wait a few weeks.

ledger.sentence: For a standard echocardiogram people usually need to do nothing to prepare.
ledger.note: BHF/NHS: no special preparation usually needed for standard echo.

ledger.sentence: The exception is the throat version, which may require avoiding eating for several hours.
ledger.note: NHS: may need to avoid eating for several hours before TOE.

ledger.sentence: The most common type is a transthoracic echocardiogram, in which a probe is placed over the chest.
ledger.note: NHS: most common type, transducer on chest.

ledger.sentence: A stress echocardiogram is done during exercise or after a medicine that has a similar effect on the heart.
ledger.note: NHS: treadmill/bike or medicine with similar effect.

ledger.sentence: A transoesophageal echocardiogram passes a probe down the throat and gives more detailed pictures than the standard test.
ledger.note: NHS: probe passed down throat, more detailed view.

ledger.sentence: Most people need no preparation for a standard echocardiogram, but may need to avoid eating for several hours before the throat version.
ledger.note: NHS: no special prep for standard; fasting for several hours may be needed for TOE.

ledger.sentence: For a standard echocardiogram no preparation is needed, and NHS trust leaflets say people can eat and drink as normal before and afterwards.
ledger.note: UHCW leaflet: no special preparation, take medication and eat and drink as normal; East Sussex and Essex leaflets agree on eating and drinking.

ledger.sentence: The person lies on their left side while a cardiac physiologist, a specially trained technician, scans the chest after putting gel on it.
ledger.note: Southampton (UHS) leaflet: lie on left side, probe with gel on chest. Cardiac physiologist performing the scan is in the Sussex leaflet; 'technician' is a plain gloss.

ledger.sentence: The physiologist may ask the person to change position or to hold their breath briefly so that the pictures are clearer.
ledger.note: Sussex leaflet: 'The cardiac physiologist may ask you to change positions or hold your breath briefly. This will help them to get better images.'

ledger.sentence: One trust leaflet describes a standard echocardiogram as painless, with no side effects and no radiation.
ledger.note: Retrieved leaflets say painless, no side effects, no radioactivity (Southampton) and low risk; the phrase 'no meaningful risks' was not found.

ledger.sentence: A stress echocardiogram checks how the heart copes with a greater workload, by taking pictures at rest and again under stress.
ledger.note: Stress echo leaflets: pictures taken at rest and again after the heart rate is increased, then compared.

ledger.sentence: The stress usually comes from walking on a treadmill or, in a dobutamine stress echocardiogram, from a medicine called dobutamine that raises the heart rate.
ledger.note: Leaflets retrieved describe treadmill exercise or the drug dobutamine to raise heart rate. Exercise bike, 'into a vein' and 'cannot exercise' wording not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: A cardiologist or a specially trained cardiac physiologist supervises the test.
ledger.note: Gloucestershire leaflet: 'supervised by a Cardiologist and/or a specially trained Cardiac Physiologist'.

ledger.sentence: Some trust leaflets ask people to avoid certain heart medicines, such as beta blockers, before a dobutamine stress echocardiogram unless the doctor advises otherwise, and each hospital gives its own instructions.
ledger.note: Plymouth leaflet asks to avoid beta blockers and calcium-channel blockers beforehand unless the doctor says otherwise; a research source notes some centres do not interrupt beta blockers. The stated mechanism was not in a retrieved leaflet.

ledger.sentence: Leaflets describe rare complications such as an abnormal heart rhythm and quote different figures, for example around 1 in 1,000 patients in one leaflet and around 1 in 500 in another.
ledger.note: Leaflets cite rare abnormal rhythm at different rates (about 1 in 1,000 in one, about 1 in 500 in another). 'Very safe' and allergic reactions not found.

ledger.sentence: A cardiac physiologist analyses the recorded images and writes a report for the doctor who requested the test.
ledger.note: Sussex leaflet: recorded images analysed by a cardiac physiologist who writes a report and sends it to the requesting doctor.

ledger.sentence: The doctor who requested the test then receives the report and passes on the results, for example at a clinic appointment or by letter, depending on the trust.
ledger.note: Leaflets say results go to the requesting clinician, possibly heard at the next clinic visit, or via a letter to the GP with a copy to the patient. Telephone not found.

ledger.sentence: One trust leaflet says the letter about stress echocardiogram results, sent to the GP with a copy to the patient, can take about two to four weeks.
ledger.note: Ashford and St Peters: letter to GP with copy to patient, taking about 2-4 weeks. A comparison with standard echo results was not retrieved.
